concept.name: Deleveraging
concept.definition: The reduction of leverage — paying down debt or shrinking positions relative to equity — by a trader, firm, or, in aggregate, an economy; at the portfolio level it means cutting gross exposure to lower the amplification of gains and losses.
concept.intuition: Leverage multiplies both ways; deleveraging is deliberately shrinking the multiplier, usually after losses, in order to survive.
concept.mechanics: Raise cash by selling assets or reducing derivatives notionals and use it to repay borrowing or release margin. Forced deleveraging after drawdowns or margin hikes is self-reinforcing across participants: everyone selling into falling markets pushes prices lower, triggering further deleveraging in loss and margin spirals.
concept.formula: Leverage after deleveraging: L' = (debt or exposure) / equity, reduced by selling assets or adding equity; the target is often set by margin requirements or risk limits.
concept.failure_modes: Synchronized deleveraging is a systemic amplifier: asset sales depress prices, which erodes equity, which forces more sales — the dynamic formalized in liquidity-spiral models. Individually, deleveraging locks in losses and forfeits the recovery.
concept.misconceptions: Deleveraging is usually involuntary, driven by lenders and margin calls rather than foresight, and during such episodes it is selling pressure — not fundamental revaluation — that dominates prices.
concept.example: A fund running 5x gross exposure that suffers a 20% drawdown and sees prime-broker margins raised might cut positions to 2x, selling into a falling market and mechanically worsening its own marks.

citations.source: Brunnermeier, M. and Pedersen, L.: Market Liquidity and Funding Liquidity (Review of Financial Studies)
citations.section: Liquidity spirals (margin spiral and loss spiral)
